llm.summary: This is a coherent Outlit integration skill, but users should handle customer data and credentials carefully.

dimensions.detail: The skill's capabilities match its stated purpose: Outlit customer intelligence, timelines, facts, source records, read-only SQL analytics, notifications, and integration setup. These involve sensitive customer and business data, but that access is disclosed and central to the integration.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions include meaningful scope limits: use high-level tools first, request only needed fields, keep SQL read-only, call schema before SQL, and send notifications only when the user explicitly asks.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The metadata declares npm and Homebrew installs for the Outlit CLI. The documentation also includes a curl-to-bash fast install path, which is disclosed but less reviewable than package-manager installation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requiring the Outlit CLI, OUTLIT_API_KEY, OAuth/MCP, and provider credentials is proportionate for connecting customer intelligence systems, but users should expect network access to Outlit and configured integrations.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses stored credentials, agent onboarding that can install the Outlit skill, and integration setup/sync behavior. It does not show hidden background execution, destructive removal actions, or automatic notification posting.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install this only if you trust Outlit and want your agent to access customer intelligence data. Prefer npm or Homebrew over the curl-to-bash installer, use browser/OAuth or environment-based credential handling where possible, and only run integration setup or notification commands when you intentionally want those account-level actions.
llm.findings:
[SQP-2] expected: The credential examples are part of disclosed auth and integration setup, so they are purpose-aligned; however, users should avoid placing real secrets directly in shell commands because those may be captured in history, logs, process listings, or agent transcripts.
[SQP-2] expected: The remote install script is a disclosed convenience installer and npm/Homebrew alternatives are provided; this is a supply-chain caution, not evidence of hidden or malicious artifact behavior.
